summary:
THE SHIPPED DEFAULTS ARE 13 LEVERS AND THEY READ, IN DECLARATION ORDER (src/opt/levers.py::OPTLevers, confirmed by assembling and printing the frozen Config): lr=2e-3; weight_decay=0.0 (OFF); grad_clip=0.0 (OFF); lr_sched='cosine' (choices cosine|none); lr_warmup=1000 Steps; lr_wavelength=0 (the sentinel: one wavelength spans the run); lr_min_frac=0.05; lr_restarts=True; lr_restart_damp=0.5; lr_decay=1.0; lr_shift_warm=0 (OFF); batch_windows=1 Window; accum=1 Backward. One wire arrives, d_effective_batch_windows=1. So ON by default: the cosine, the 1000-step warmup, the 5% floor, the restart switch and the full envelope. OFF by default: weight decay, gradient clipping, the self-inflicted-shift re-warm; and INERT-BY-ARITHMETIC by default: restarts, damping and the envelope, because the 0 sentinel fits exactly one cycle.

THE HEADLINE ANSWER TO THE RESTART QUESTION IS THAT THE LEDGER GETS IT RIGHT. At the shipped defaults over 1000 windows the restart arm reads 'Gate opt.lr.restarts: UNREACHABLE (1 vs > 1 cycle) -- OPT_LR_RESTARTS is on and exactly ONE cycle fits: OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=0 against a horizon of 1000 steps (the 0 sentinel makes one wavelength span the whole run), so the schedule is bit-identical to restarts=off and no restart can occur.' The armed-but-inert-reported-as-armed defect the assignment predicted is NOT present on that arm, and neither is it on damping, envelope, re-warm, clip or weight decay: all six read UNREACHABLE with a true reason naming their lever and value. Driven the other way (OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=300 over a 1000-step horizon, 4 cycles) the curve genuinely wraps -- 5.00% of peak at step 324, 86.09% at 325 -- restarts and damping fire, and the damping visibly scales the whole following cycle while the floor stays exactly lr*lr_min_frac (5.00% of peak at every pre-wrap step at every damp value tested).

THE DEFECT IS ONE LEVEL UP: THE SCHED GATE IS NOT WIRED TO THE GATES IT DISABLES. At OPT_LR_SCHED=none -- the one-flag ablation for this project's leading Goal-A hypothesis, the arm the owner will actually run -- src/opt/api.py::_schedule returns the flat peak on its first line and the warmup, wavelength, floor, restarts, damping, envelope and re-warm are all structurally dead. NOT ONE of the seven says so. Three of them positively lie: at OPT_LR_SCHED=none OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=300 OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM=50 with a shift supplied, the ledger prints 'Gate opt.lr.restarts: armed, did not fire (0 vs 4 cycles fitted)', 'Gate opt.lr.decay: armed, did not fire (0 vs decay=1.0)' and 'Gate opt.lr.shift_warm: armed, did not fire (0 vs 1 notification(s) x 50 steps)' -- three mechanisms that CANNOT fire, printed in the words reserved for a measurement, with fabricated arithmetic beside them (there are no cycles and no envelope in a flat schedule). Two more mechanisms, the warmup and the floor, have NO GATE AT ALL in any configuration.

SECOND, THE UNREACHABLE ARMS HARDCODE fired=False INSTEAD OF READING THEIR OWN COUNTER, WHICH DISARMS spine/gate.py::Gate's OWN REFUSAL. Gate.__post_init__ raises on 'unreachable AND fired' precisely to stop a report carrying both; counters() passes the literal False, so the refusal can never trip and the ledger can and does carry both. At PURE SHIPPED DEFAULTS ON BOTH SIDES of a resume, lengthening the run from 1000 to 2000 windows makes the first resumed step jump from the restored lr_prev=1.0e-4 to 1.21e-3 (12.1x), the detector calls it a cosine restart, opt.restart.detected reads 1 -- in the same ledger that prints 'no restart can occur'. That StepOutcome.restart is one of the three self-inflicted-shift stamps spine/compose.py feeds FAB.grow_check, so it also tells the growth controller a self-inflicted shift landed on exactly the first step after the boundary: ISSUES P1-H17's shape, returning through the horizon instead of through the counter that was checkpointed to kill it.

THIRD, AND THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST IF THE SCHEDULE HYPOTHESIS IS EVER TESTED WITH RESTARTS ON: THE CLOSED LOOP SWITCHES ITSELF OFF. The detector's second condition, lr > 0.5*opt.lr, is exactly what the damping (and the envelope) drive the restart peak below. An undamped wrap is priced at min_frac + (1-min_frac)*restart_amp of peak, so detection needs restart_amp > (0.5-0.05)/0.95 = 0.4737. At the shipped lr_restart_damp=0.5 that permits at most TWO dampings ever; at any damp <= 0.4737 exactly ONE. Measured over a 7-cycle run with the envelope off: damp=0.9 -> 6 of 6 wraps detected, 5 damped; damp=0.5 -> 3 of 6 detected, 2 damped, restart_amp latched at 0.25 with three real wraps (5.0% -> 28.75% of peak) invisible to the counter and to the loop; damp=0.4 and damp=0.2 -> 2 of 6 detected, ONE damping, then permanently blind. The stronger the damping an operator asks for, the fewer times it can be applied, and the gate prints 'FIRED (3 vs 7 cycles fitted)' with nothing saying three restarts went unseen. The lever's own promise in src/opt/levers.py -- 'a schedule whose restarts keep failing anneals ITSELF off within two or three of them' -- is false for every value at or below 0.4737.

Suite green throughout; nothing I did could move it, since I edited nothing.

findings.detail: AT OPT_LR_SCHED=none NOT ONE OF THE SEVEN DISABLED MECHANISMS READS UNREACHABLE FOR THAT REASON, AND THREE READ 'armed, did not fire'. src/opt/api.py::_schedule opens with `if sched == "none": return float(lr), (False, False, False, False)`, so the warmup ramp, the wavelength, the lr_min_frac floor, the restart wrap, the damping, the envelope and the shift re-warm are all structurally unreachable -- exactly what src/opt/levers.py::OPTLevers says on lr_sched ('the warmup, the wavelength, the floor, the restarts, the damping, the envelope and the re-warm are ALL structurally unreachable ... the old tree printed every one of them on the EFFECTIVE line as though it had applied. The gate must print its own predicate'). counters() builds every downstream gate from n_cycles, lr_decay, lr_shift_warm and the counters, and NEVER from `sched`; the string is read once, for the opt.lr.sched gate itself, and its consequences are wired to nothing. Measured at OPT_LR_SCHED=none OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=300 OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM=50 with a shift supplied once, over 1000 windows, every rate flat at 0.002: 'Gate opt.lr.restarts: armed, did not fire (0 vs 4 cycles fitted)'; 'Gate opt.lr.decay: armed, did not fire (0 vs decay=1.0)'; 'Gate opt.lr.shift_warm: armed, did not fire (0 vs 1 notification(s) x 50 steps)'. All three are the words spine/gate.py::Gate reserves for 'the mechanism ran and its condition was not met -- a measurement', printed for mechanisms with no code path, and all three carry arithmetic that does not exist in a flat schedule (there are no cycles, no envelope, and the re-warm line positively invites the reader to conclude that a shift WAS notified and lr_shift_warm declined to act on it). The fourth, opt.lr.restart_damp, reads UNREACHABLE with a FALSE reason -- see the separate opt.restart.readings finding. The remaining two, the warmup and the floor, have no Gate at all in any configuration. At the DEFAULT wavelength the same run prints UNREACHABLE on restarts/damp/decay for the CYCLE-FIT reason rather than for the ablation, which is a true sentence about the wrong cause: it tells an operator to go change OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH when the schedule is switched off. Note the shipped-defaults ledger is otherwise correct, so this is a defect that appears only on the arm the schedule hypothesis is tested on.

Contrast the SAME wavelength under the shipped cosine (drop only OPT_LR_SCHED): 'Gate opt.lr.restarts: FIRED (2 vs 4 cycles fitted)', 'Gate opt.lr.decay: FIRED (901 vs decay=1.0)', and with OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM=5 plus a shift at step 200, 'Gate opt.lr.shift_warm: FIRED (4 vs 1 notification(s) x 5 steps)'. Both states of all three gates run and quoted.

findings.detail: A PHANTOM COSINE RESTART ON THE FIRST STEP AFTER A RESUME AT A LONGER RUN, AT PURE SHIPPED DEFAULTS ON BOTH SIDES OF THE BOUNDARY, IN THE SAME LEDGER THAT SAYS NO RESTART CAN OCCUR. src/opt/api.py::load_state restores st.lr_prev verbatim and explicitly BLESSES a changed horizon ('the horizon changed across the boundary and the LIVE one is in force ... which is the legitimate case'). The detector is `st.lr_prev > 0 and lr > 1.5 * st.lr_prev and lr > 0.5 * opt.lr`, and a resume that lengthens the run re-prices the SAME step against a longer horizon, which moves the rate UP by more than 1.5x whenever the parent ended deep in the anneal -- which is what a completed run always is, because the cosine ends at the floor. Measured: parent 1000 windows at the defaults, checkpoint at opt_step=1000 with lr_prev=1.0e-4 (5.00% of peak); child at the defaults with run_windows=2000; first resumed step is priced at 1.2133e-3 (60.7% of peak, a 12.1x jump) and StepOutcome.restart is True. THREE CONSEQUENCES. (a) opt.restart.detected reads 1 while the same counters() call prints 'Gate opt.lr.restarts: UNREACHABLE (1 vs > 1 cycle) -- ... so the schedule is bit-identical to restarts=off and no restart can occur.' (b) StepOutcome.restart is one of the three self-inflicted-shift stamps spine/compose.py's LOOP_ORDER feeds FAB.grow_check ('the E draw row's resample, the B TOK.mint_burst retok, and OPT's LR restart'), so the growth controller is told 'this loss jump is OURS' on exactly the first step after a resume -- which is the shape src/opt/api.py::maybe_step's own docstring says lr_prev was checkpointed to kill ('every resume reported a cosine restart on its second step ... which told the growth controller the loss jump was self-inflicted ON EXACTLY THE STEP A NEW AREA ARRIVES', ISSUES P1-H17). Checkpointing lr_prev closed the counter route and left the horizon route open. (c) With st.cycle_best also restored, the closed loop can damp on this phantom restart. The rate change itself is legitimate; the RESTART CLASSIFICATION of it is not, and no state distinguishes 'the cosine wrapped' from 'the horizon moved under a resumed step'. The sharper variant: resume the same checkpoint with OPT_LR_SCHED=none OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=300 and the ledger prints 'Gate opt.lr.sched: armed, did not fire (none ...)' and 'Gate opt.lr.restarts: FIRED (1 vs 18 cycles fitted)' side by side, with every rate flat at 0.002.
findings.repro: Phase 1 at the shipped defaults: build with run_windows=units.Windows(1000), run 1000 scaled_backward+maybe_step pairs, saved=state_dict -> saved['opt_step']=1000, saved['lr_prev']=0.0001. Phase 2 at the shipped defaults, run_windows=units.Windows(2000): load_state(...).restored is True with the 'horizon changed ... legitimate case' reason; the first maybe_step returns StepOutcome(stepped=True, lr=0.0012133326452654389, restart=True, damped=False); counters() then reports opt.restart.detected=1 beside 'Gate opt.lr.restarts: UNREACHABLE (1 vs > 1 cycle) -- ... no restart can occur.' THE NEGATIVE CASE: run the same phase 2 with run_windows=units.Windows(1000) (the horizon unchanged) and restart is False, opt.restart.detected=0 -- the gate and the counter agree.

findings.detail: THE RESTART DETECTOR GOES BLIND EXACTLY WHEN THE DAMPING WORKS, SO THE CLOSED LOOP CAPS AT TWO APPLICATIONS AT THE SHIPPED DAMP AND AT ONE FOR ANY STRONGER SETTING. Detection requires `lr > 0.5 * opt.lr`; src/opt/api.py::_schedule prices a wrap as `cyc = min_frac + (cyc - min_frac) * restart_amp` with cyc=1.0 at the wrap, i.e. min_frac + (1-min_frac)*restart_amp of peak. With the shipped lr_min_frac=0.05 that clears the bar only while restart_amp > (0.5-0.05)/0.95 = 0.4737. Since st.restart_amp is only ever multiplied INSIDE `if restart:`, once a wrap falls under the bar no restart is detected, st.cycle_best is never updated again and st.restart_amp is frozen for the rest of the run -- the mechanism disables its own input. MEASURED over a 7-cycle run (1000 -> 4000 windows, OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=610 OPT_LR_WARMUP=10 OPT_LR_DECAY=0.0 so the envelope is out of it, Reading(2.4, seeds=3) every step so every cycle loses): six real wraps, each jumping from 5.0% of peak to the value shown. damp=0.9 -> 6 detected, 5 damped, amp 0.59049. damp=0.5 (SHIPPED) -> 3 detected, 2 damped, amp latched at 0.25, wraps 4/5/6 all at 28.75% of peak and invisible. damp=0.4 -> 2 detected, ONE damping, amp 0.40. damp=0.2 -> 2 detected, ONE damping, amp 0.20. The lever is inverted in its own strength parameter: the harder an operator damps, the fewer times the damping can be applied. src/opt/levers.py::OPTLevers promises the opposite -- 'Cumulative damping means a schedule whose restarts keep failing anneals ITSELF off within two or three of them' -- which is false at every damp <= 0.4737. THE ENVELOPE DOES THE SAME THING ON ITS OWN at the shipped lr_decay=1.0: the envelope multiplier passes 0.5 at about 52% of the run, so with the envelope on and one damping applied every wrap past ~14% of the run is undetectable (measured at OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=300 over 1000 steps: wraps at 325/550/775, only 325 and 550 detected, 775 priced at 9.93% of peak). AND THE LEDGER GIVES NO SIGN: 'Gate opt.lr.restarts: FIRED (3 vs 7 cycles fitted)' is the only line, and a reader has no way to tell 3-of-6-wraps-seen from 3-restarts-happened. The detector arithmetic matches the frozen maybe_step docstring character for character, so this is a consequence nobody wrote down rather than a P4 deviation -- reporting, not proposing an edit, because the fix (count wraps from the cycle index rather than from the rate ratio, or floor the bar on restart_amp) changes what a restart MEANS and is the owner's call.
findings.repro: For damp in (0.9, 0.5, 0.4, 0.2): assemble with {'OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH':'610','OPT_LR_WARMUP':'10','OPT_LR_DECAY':'0.0','OPT_LR_RESTART_DAMP':damp}, build with run_windows=units.Windows(4000), drive 4000 windows passing best_bpb=Reading(2.4, seed_count=3) every step. n_cycles=7, warmup=10, per_c=570.0, so the wraps are steps 580/1150/1720/2290/2860/3430 and the step before each is at 5.0% of peak in every arm. Detected/damped/final restart_amp/rate at each wrap (% of peak): 0.9 -> 6/5/0.59049/[100,100,90.5,81.95,74.26,67.33]; 0.5 -> 3/2/0.25/[100,100,52.5,28.75,28.75,28.75]; 0.4 -> 2/1/0.40/[100,100,43,43,43,43]; 0.2 -> 2/1/0.20/[100,100,24,24,24,24]. The FIRING state of the same gate: 'Gate opt.lr.restarts: FIRED (3 vs 7 cycles fitted)' and 'Gate opt.lr.restart_damp: FIRED (2 vs damp=0.5, refused_n1=0)'. The CANNOT-FIRE state at the shipped defaults: 'Gate opt.lr.restarts: UNREACHABLE (1 vs > 1 cycle) -- ... no restart can occur.'

findings.detail: EVERY UNREACHABLE ARM PASSES A LITERAL fired=False INSTEAD OF ITS OWN COUNTER, WHICH DISARMS spine/gate.py::Gate's ONLY SELF-CHECK, AND load_state THEN CARRIES COUNTERS ACROSS A BOUNDARY WHERE THE LEVERS CHANGED. spine/gate.py::Gate.__post_init__ raises ValueError on 'declared unreachable AND fired ... a report carrying both says nothing' -- the record's one guard against exactly this collapse. counters() writes `Gate('opt.lr.restarts', False, n_cycles, ...)`, `Gate('opt.lr.restart_damp', False, damp, ...)`, `Gate('opt.lr.decay', False, decay, ...)`, `Gate('opt.lr.shift_warm', False, shift_warm, ...)` and `Gate('opt.clip.applied', False, 0, ...)` on their unreachable arms, so the guard is structurally untrippable and the contradiction is printed instead of refused. It is not hypothetical: src/opt/api.py::load_state restores every counter except opt.build.* ('A mechanism that fired 4,000 times before the boundary must not read "armed but 0" after it'), while every reachability predicate in counters() is computed from the LIVE Config alone. Resuming a run that had clipping, a re-warm and four cycles into a run at the shipped defaults prints, in one ledger: opt.lr.envelope_applied=901 beside 'Gate opt.lr.decay: UNREACHABLE ... off BY ARITHMETIC'; opt.lr.shift_warm_applied=4 and opt.shift.notifications=1 beside 'Gate opt.lr.shift_warm: UNREACHABLE (0 vs > 0) -- OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM=0'; opt.restart.detected=2 beside 'Gate opt.lr.restarts: UNREACHABLE ... no restart can occur.' A SIXTH SYMPTOM IS SILENT DATA LOSS: 'opt.clip.applied' is BOTH a counter key and a Gate name, and the last lines of counters() do `ledger[g.name] = g`, so the Gate overwrites the counter in the returned dict. On the clip-off arm the Gate carries the literal 0, so a restored count of 1000 clipped steps is erased from the ledger entirely (st.counters still holds 1000; the ledger the report reads says 0). The same collision exists on 'opt.encoder_steps_here' but is harmless there because that Gate passes the real counter.
findings.repro: Parent: assemble {'OPT_GRAD_CLIP':'0.001','OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM':'5','OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH':'300'}, build at run_windows=units.Windows(1000), drive 1000 windows with best_bpb=Reading(2.4,3) and one shift_at=units.Steps(400); st.counters -> clip.applied=1000, lr.shift_warm_applied=4, lr.envelope_applied=901, restart.detected=2; saved=state_dict. Child: assemble {} (shipped defaults), build at run_windows=units.Windows(1000), load_state(saved).restored is True, take 3 steps, call counters(). ledger['opt.lr.envelope_applied']=901, ledger['opt.lr.shift_warm_applied']=4, ledger['opt.restart.detected']=2, ledger['opt.shift.notifications']=1 -- and the gate lines are the four UNREACHABLE ones quoted above. ledger['opt.clip.applied'] is the Gate object printing 'UNREACHABLE (0 vs n/a)' while st.counters['opt.clip.applied'] is 1000. THE NON-CONTRADICTING STATE: the same child WITHOUT the load_state prints the identical four UNREACHABLE lines with every one of those counters at 0, which is the reading a reader would take at face value in both cases.

findings.detail: opt.restart.readings IS NOT THE MIRROR OF opt.shift.notifications IT IS DOCUMENTED AS, SO THE restart_damp GATE PRINTS A FALSE SENTENCE ON ITS UNREACHABLE ARM. The counter's own entry in src/opt/api.py::maybe_step's DID IT FIRE block says it is 'the mirror of opt.shift.notifications on the other runtime argument ... nothing at RUNTIME can tell a run where no Reading ever arrived from a run where every Reading said the cycle paid. This is the count that makes that declared UNREACHABLE checkable instead of asserted.' The two are not mirrors. opt.shift.notifications is incremented on ARRIVAL, at the very top of maybe_step and deliberately outside the due-ness check. opt.restart.readings is incremented inside `if restart:` -- only when a restart has already been detected -- so it counts Readings CONSUMED, and reads 0 on every run where no restart fires no matter how many Readings arrived. counters() then renders `elif readings == 0:` as 'Gate opt.lr.restart_damp: UNREACHABLE (0.5 vs < 1.0 on a losing cycle) -- no Reading has ever arrived (opt.restart.readings == 0), so the held-out measurement the damping judges a cycle by does not exist.' That is a statement of fact about another package's output, printed on the arm spine/gate.py::Gate demands a reason for, and it is false whenever EVAL is supplying Readings and no restart has happened yet -- which is the normal state of every multi-cycle run before its first wrap, and the permanent state of every OPT_LR_SCHED=none run. It sends a reader to debug EVAL for a condition OPT's own detector caused. The true statement on that arm is 'no restart has been detected, so the damping has had no cycle to judge'.
findings.repro: Assemble {'OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH':'300'} (shipped cosine, 4 cycles fitted over a 1000-step horizon), build at run_windows=units.Windows(1000) but drive only 200 windows -- i.e. stop before the first wrap at step 325 -- passing best_bpb=Reading(2.4, seed_count=3) on every one of the 200 steps. counters() prints 'Gate opt.lr.restart_damp: UNREACHABLE (0.5 vs < 1.0 on a losing cycle) -- no Reading has ever arrived (opt.restart.readings == 0) ...' with ledger['opt.restart.readings']=0 and ledger['opt.restart.detected']=0, after 200 Readings arrived. THE OTHER STATE: drive the full 1000 windows with the same Readings and the gate reads 'FIRED (1 vs damp=0.5, refused_n1=0)' with readings=2 -- so the counter only ever equals the number of DETECTED RESTARTS, never the number of Readings.

findings.detail: THE WARMUP, THE COSINE FLOOR AND THE WAVELENGTH HAVE NO GATE IN ANY CONFIGURATION, AND THE WARMUP IS STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE ON EVERY SHORT RUN WHILE THE REPORT PRINTS A WARMUP LENGTH. counters()'s gate list is opt.accum.invariant, opt.lr.sched, opt.build.grad_clip, opt.clip.applied, opt.lr.restarts, opt.lr.restart_damp, opt.lr.decay, opt.lr.shift_warm, opt.weight_decay, opt.encoder_steps_here, opt.grad_norm -- eleven, and none of them is the warmup or the floor. The warmup surfaces only as the bare counter opt.lr.in_warmup and as a report line. src/opt/api.py::_schedule's warmup branch is `if step < w` with `w = max(1, int(horizon.warmup))` against a counter that src/opt/api.py::maybe_step advances to 1 before the first pricing, so at warmup=1 the branch is `1 < 1` and NO step is ever in warmup: the mechanism cannot fire, opt.lr.in_warmup prints a bare 0 indistinguishable from 'it ran and never triggered', and the report line still says 'opt.horizon: warmup=1 (asked 1000, clamped=True)'. warmup=1 covers every run of 19 or fewer optimizer steps, because build() sets `warmup_cap = max(1, total_steps // 10)` -- including the OPT_BATCH_WINDOWS=16 OPT_ACCUM=4 arm the supervisor spot-checked. At warmup=2 the one 'warmed' step is priced at (1+1)/2 = 1.0 x peak, so opt.lr.in_warmup reads 1 for a step that got the unwarmed rate. THE OFF-BY-ONE AND THE warmup=1 UNREACHABILITY WERE ALREADY REPORTED against src/opt/api.py::_schedule in .rework/audits/v_opt_units.json and I confirmed both independently (run_windows 15/20/1000 -> warmup 1/2/100, in_warmup 0/1/99, first rate 0.002/0.002/4e-05); what is NEW here and belongs to this lens is that there is no Gate to carry the third state at all, so the repair for that finding has no record to write into. The lr_min_frac floor has neither a Gate nor a counter, so 'the schedule never returned zero' is unattested in the ledger, and at OPT_LR_SCHED=none the floor is bypassed with nothing saying so.
findings.repro: At the shipped defaults, build at run_windows=units.Windows(N) and drive N windows: N=15 -> horizon.warmup=1, opt.lr.in_warmup=0, first rate 0.002 (100% of peak), report line 'opt.horizon: warmup=1 (asked 1000, clamped=True)'; N=20 -> warmup=2, in_warmup=1, first rate still 0.002; N=1000 -> warmup=100, in_warmup=99, first rate 4e-05 (2% of peak). In all three, [k for k,v in counters(...).items() if isinstance(v, Gate) and ('warm' in k or 'min' in k or 'floor' in k)] == ['opt.lr.shift_warm'] -- the re-warm, not the warmup. Grep src/opt/api.py for Gate( : eleven constructions, none naming a warmup or a floor.

findings.detail: opt.encoder_steps_here IS AN UNTRIPPABLE GUARD: NOTHING IN THE TREE INCREMENTS IT, SO ITS GATE CAN ONLY EVER PRINT 'armed, did not fire' AND THE REGRESSION IT NAMES WOULD RETURN SILENTLY ANYWAY. `grep -rn encoder_steps_here src/` returns exactly four source lines: the initialisation to 0 in src/opt/api.py::build's counters dict, two lines of prose in src/opt/api.py::maybe_step's docstring, the Gate construction in src/opt/api.py::counters, and one mention in src/spine/compose.py's prose. There is no `+= 1` anywhere, and `grep -rn 'encoder.step()\|encoder.zero_grad' src/` returns nothing. The Gate's own reason says 'A nonzero value is the double step returning -- SIG.train_step on SIG's cadence and this flush gate both stepping the encoder ... it returns silently because both call sites look correct in isolation'. If that regression returned, the counter would still be 0, because the only thing that could raise it is the very edit that introduces the defect. This is the shape the spine names as 60 of the survey's 475 records ('guards whose condition could not be satisfied at all') and it is printed in the armed-and-inert words. It is a deliberate tripwire read backwards, and the docstring is honest that 'armed, did not fire' IS the passing state -- which is why I file it medium rather than high -- but a tripwire that cannot trip is not a check, and the honest render for it is a Gate whose value is derived from something observable (st.encoder's step count, or len(st.encoder.state) which AdamW grows on its first step) rather than from a counter with no writer.
findings.repro: cd /home/user/LLM-Test && grep -rn 'encoder_steps_here' src/ --include=*.py -> four hits, all in src/opt/api.py::build (the `"opt.encoder_steps_here": 0` entry in its counters dict), src/opt/api.py::maybe_step (two lines of its DID IT FIRE docstring block) and src/opt/api.py::counters (the Gate construction), plus one prose mention in src/spine/compose.py::<module>. No assignment, no increment. In every configuration I drove -- shipped defaults, OPT_LR_SCHED=none, 4-cycle, 7-cycle, clip on, clip off, accum=4 -- the line is byte-identical: 'Gate opt.encoder_steps_here: armed, did not fire (0 vs 0) -- Q-OPT-6 REGRESSION COUNTER, READ BACKWARDS ...'. There is no configuration of the shipped tree in which it reads anything else, which is the finding.

findings.detail: THE RESTART PEAK THE DAMPING IS NAMED FOR IS DELIVERED UNDAMPED. src/opt/api.py::maybe_step prices the step first (`lr = lr_at(opt, st, st.opt_step)`), detects the restart from that rate, and only then does `st.restart_amp *= float(opt.lr_restart_damp)`. So the multiplier lands from the step AFTER the wrap: the wrap itself is priced at full amplitude for one optimizer step. src/opt/levers.py::OPTLevers describes the lever as a 'Multiplier on the next restart's swing', and the swing's own step is the one it does not multiply. Measured with the envelope off (OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=610 OPT_LR_WARMUP=10 OPT_LR_DECAY=0.0, damp=0.5, losing Readings): the wrap at step 1150 that TRIGGERS the first damping is itself priced at 100.0% of peak; the following cycle and the wrap at 1720 are at 52.5%. The ordering is forced -- the detector infers a restart from the rate ratio, so the undamped rate must exist before the verdict can -- so this is a structural residue rather than a slip, and the bulk of each cycle IS damped. It is worth a line in the report rather than a repair, since a reader comparing st.restart_amp against the rate at the wrap will find them inconsistent by exactly one step and has nothing telling them why.
findings.repro: In the damp sweep above, damp=0.5: outcomes with restart=True at steps 580/1150/1720; outcomes with damped=True at 1150/1720. Rate at step 1150 = 0.002 (100.0% of peak) on the step whose own outcome carries damped=True; rate at 1151 onwards is scaled by 0.5 above the floor. Same shape at damp=0.9 (wraps 1150 and 1720 both priced 100.0% while damped=True first appears at 1150).

findings.detail: UNDER OPT_LR_RESTARTS=off THE DAMPING AND ENVELOPE GATES NAME THE CYCLE COUNT AS THE CAUSE AND NOT THE SWITCH THAT SET IT. src/opt/api.py::build forces `n_cycles = 1` in the `else` of `if bool(opt.lr_restarts)`, so at OPT_LR_RESTARTS=off the cycle count is 1 by decree rather than by fit. counters() then routes opt.lr.restart_damp and opt.lr.decay through their `n_cycles <= 1` arms and prints 'only 1 cycle(s) fit this run, so OPT_LR_RESTART_DAMP=0.5 is off BY ARITHMETIC' and 'the envelope is gated on n_cycles > 1 and 1 cycle(s) fit, so OPT_LR_DECAY=1.0 is off BY ARITHMETIC'. Both sentences are true and both point at the wrong lever: with OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=300 against a 1000-step horizon four cycles WOULD have fitted, and an operator reading these two lines is told to go change the wavelength they already set. spine/gate.py::Gate requires the reason to say why 'not merely that', and the why here is OPT_LR_RESTARTS=off -- which the gate immediately above them does say, so the information exists one line away and is not carried down. Low because no reading is false and the neighbouring line repairs it for an attentive reader.
findings.repro: Assemble {'OPT_LR_RESTARTS':'off','OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH':'300'}, build at run_windows=units.Windows(1000), drive 1000 windows: 'Gate opt.lr.restarts: UNREACHABLE (1 vs > 1 cycle) -- OPT_LR_RESTARTS=off, so the cosine holds at the floor after one cycle and no restart exists to detect.' immediately followed by 'Gate opt.lr.restart_damp: UNREACHABLE (0.5 vs < 1.0 past cycle 0) -- the damping is gated on cycle_index > 0 and only 1 cycle(s) fit this run ...' and 'Gate opt.lr.decay: UNREACHABLE (1.0 vs > 0.0 and n_cycles > 1) -- ... and 1 cycle(s) fit ...'. Drop OPT_LR_RESTARTS and the same wavelength gives n_cycles=4 and both gates become live.

findings.detail: THE SHIPPED-DEFAULTS LEDGER IS RIGHT, INCLUDING THE RESTART CASE THE ASSIGNMENT SINGLED OUT. lr_restarts is a boolean defaulting to True and n_cycles is fitted, so at the 0 sentinel one wavelength spans the run and the mechanism restarts nothing while switched on -- and the ledger SAYS SO rather than printing a zero: 'Gate opt.lr.restarts: UNREACHABLE (1 vs > 1 cycle) -- OPT_LR_RESTARTS is on and exactly ONE cycle fits: OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=0 against a horizon of 1000 steps (the 0 sentinel makes one wavelength span the whole run), so the schedule is bit-identical to restarts=off and no restart can occur.' The damping and the envelope follow it with their own 'off BY ARITHMETIC rather than armed and inert' reasons, which is the distinction ISSUES.md PART 4 files as the canonical case, correctly made. Six further gates were run in BOTH states and every reading is right: opt.build.grad_clip UNREACHABLE at 0.0 / FIRED at 1000.0; opt.clip.applied UNREACHABLE at clip=0 ('This is not "armed and did not fire"') / 'armed, did not fire (0 vs max-norm 1000.0)' when armed and nothing exceeded / 'FIRED (40 vs max-norm 0.001)' when everything did -- all three states of that one gate distinguished; opt.weight_decay UNREACHABLE at 0.0 / FIRED at 0.01; opt.lr.shift_warm UNREACHABLE at 0 / UNREACHABLE with the different 'NOBODY IS SUPPLYING shift_at' reason at 5 with no notification / FIRED (4 vs 1 notification(s) x 5 steps) when notified -- again three distinct states; opt.grad_norm UNREACHABLE when no step was ever taken ('This is "never reached", not "measured 0.0"') / FIRED with p50 and p99 when steps were; opt.lr.decay UNREACHABLE at decay=0.0 with the pre-2026-08-26 reason / UNREACHABLE at n_cycles=1 / FIRED (901 vs decay=1.0) at n_cycles=4. THE MULTI-CYCLE SCHEDULE ITSELF IS ALSO CORRECT where it is reachable: at OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=300 over a 1000-step horizon the curve genuinely wraps (step 324 = 5.00% of peak, step 325 = 86.09%), the damping applies across the restart to the whole following cycle (step 550 = 52.50%, step 551 = 27.47%), the first wrap is correctly NOT damped because st.cycle_best is None and there is no inherited best to fail against, and the floor holds exactly at lr*lr_min_frac = 5.00% of peak at every pre-wrap step at every damp value tested (0.9/0.5/0.4/0.2) -- the property lr_at's docstring asserts, true post-warmup at n_cycles 1, 4 and 7.
findings.repro: Shipped defaults, run_windows=units.Windows(1000), 1000 windows driven: the eleven gate lines quoted above, opt.horizon warmup=100 wavelength=1000 (from the 0 sentinel=True) cycles_fitted=1, opt.backward=1000 opt.step=1000 opt.lr.writes.base=1000 opt.lr.writes.encoder=1000 opt.grad_norm.samples=1000 opt.encoder_steps_here=0. Each paired state was produced by re-assembling in a fresh process (lever._reopen_assembly() + rng.reset_issued() between builds) with one env var changed at a time: OPT_GRAD_CLIP in (0.0, 1000, 0.001); OPT_WEIGHT_DECAY in (0.0, 0.01); OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM in (0, 5) x (no shift_at, shift_at=units.Steps(200)); OPT_LR_DECAY in (0.0, 1.0) x OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH in (0, 300); OPT_ACCUM=4 with 2 backwards for the no-step arm.
